title: concierge-deal-acceleration-battlecard-sketch
content:
One-line summary:
A compact, sales-facing battlecard for high-touch (concierge) enterprise opportunities where procurement timelines and security reviews are the gating factors. Focus is on accelerating commitment windows by surfacing technical gating items, clear handoffs to SEs, and low-friction commercial levers.

Why this exists (problem):
- Several mid-to-large prospects are stuck in security / procurement loops despite positive POC results.
- Field needs a single-sheet resource to: articulate common objections, call out exact artifacts/security proofs customers ask for, and outline fast paths for pilots and signature.
- Current collateral is scattered across decks, Confluence pages, and PRs — reps waste cycles reinventing responses.

Primary audience:
- Account executives working on enterprise + strategic midmarket deals
- Solutions Engineers and Security SEs who join technical reviews
- Renewal/Customer Success managers preparing pre-sales handoffs

Top-line positioning bullets (30–60s):
- Redwood Inference: production-first inference platform with flexible deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). We move teams to predictable latency and unit-costs while giving enterprise controls (VPC, KMS, audit) for compliance.
- For customers needing to shorten procurement: we offer an "accelerated concierge" engagement pairing an assigned SE + expedited compliance bundle + pilot SLA.

Key value props (short):
- Predictable economics — baseline token & embedding unit pricing + reserved capacity options
- Rapid compliance artifacts — security pack (SOC2 sampling, audit checklist, network topology, KMS cert details) ready within 48–72 hours of request
- Deployment flexibility — push-button progression from hosted pilot -> dedicated capacity -> private deployment
- Fallback reliability — automated routing and rollback policies to protect SLA during rollouts

Common objections and suggested replies (concise):
- Objection: "We need on-prem / air-gapped — can Redwood do that?"
  Reply: Yes. Offer the Private deployment path; highlight customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem package. Flag SE to schedule architecture call, then reference private-deployments/airgap playbook (linked).

- Objection: "We can’t expose data to a hosted API."
  Reply: Explain private + dedicated isolation options. Offer proof points: existing customers in finance/healthcare (redacted names) running with KMS/HSM integration and per-tenant network controls. Request org-level NDA if they need references.

- Objection: "Latency requirements are strict — will you hit our P95 target?"
  Reply: Present model and infra benchmark for similar workloads (attach recent latency runbook). Offer a short canary with monitored SLOs and a guaranteed rollback plan.

Technical risk buckets (what SE should validate up front):
- Data residency and encryption: customer KMS/HSM policy, required certifications, export controls
- Network topology: inbound/outbound restrictions, proxy/NAT, private peering or IP allowlist needs
- Model footprint: sequence lengths, peak concurrent requests, KV-cache persistence expectations
- Integration surface: agent/service calling, function/tooling, streaming requirements

Handoff checklist (for AE -> SE, aim: 10 min prep):
- AE pre-fill: business use case, target personas, expected QPS and P95 target, desired go-live date
- Attach: sample prompts, a representative payload size, example PII classification (yes/no), initial test dataset (if allowed)
- Ask SE to confirm: recommended capacity tier (hosted vs dedicated), suggested quantization profile, expected infra delta for peak bursts
- Security lead: collect required artifact list (SOC2 PDFs, network diagram, KMS attestation) — link to security templated pack

Commercial acceleration levers (what AE can offer to shorten cycle):
- 90-day pilot with cap on tokens and a discounted pilot rate (internally pre-approved thresholds)
- Short-term reserved capacity trial credit (covers first month of Dedicated) — requires quick credit approval via finance
- Executive sponsor intro (VP-level) if procurement stalls — coordinate with Customer Success

Escalation map (simple):
- Day 0–7 stall on security artifact request: tag #enterprise-deals, ping Security SE rotation
- Day 7–14: engage Solutions Lead (Sofia Martinez) for architecture sign-off and draft temp mitigations
- >Day 14: request executive sponsor call and offer a short CTO-to-CTO readout

Quick templates (copy/paste):
- Email to Security Slack thread / SE: "Quick handoff: <account> is requesting SOC2 + network topology by EOD Fri. AE: <name>. SE: can you confirm ETA for artifacts? JIRA: SE-<id>."

- Customer-facing pilot offer (short):
"We can spin up a 90-day pilot with monitoring SLOs and an assigned Redwood SE. Pilot includes a security artifact pack and a documented rollback plan. If pilot shows <x> throughput and P95 targets met, we’ll provide a path to Reserved Capacity with a one-month credit to accelerate procurement."

Metrics to escalate internally (what to log in CRM):
- Time from first security artifact request to delivery
- Number of open technical questions after first SE call
- Pilot conversion rate (pilot->paid within 90 days)
- Average procurement time savings when concierge path used vs not

Open questions / TODOs (for this draft):
- Need to confirm exact contents and SLA for "security artifact pack" (Aaron to own, Jira SE-4218)
- Fast-track pricing approval process needs a documented threshold (how many USD credit can AE commit without manager approval?)
- Create a templated one-pager for CISO sign-off (privacy+crypto focused)

References & quick links:
- Private deployments playbook (confluence link placeholder)
- Recent latency bench for 8k context model (GH run id/bench results link)
- Finance fast-credit play: FIN-rapid-approval-2024 (internal doc)

Notes to self / rough sketch items (informal):
- Could we bundle a short "security bake-off" where we pre-populate a minimal audit trail for them to validate? Low effort on our side, high perceived value.
- Consider a 2–3 slide "for CISO" one-pager separate from the technical checklist — purely risk/compliance language, no product jargon.
- Add a short checklist for legal: typical contract clauses customers push back on and our standardized replies (data use, indemnities, exit data handling).

Intent for next iteration:
- Pull actual artifact pack contents and insert as bullet checklist
- Add a small decision flow graphic (AE scripting) to use in meetings
- Get approval on pilot credit thresholds from finance & ops

-- end of sketch --
